name: Alice Weidel
description: German opposition politician advocating national sovereignty, immigration restriction and market-oriented economic reform.

axes.brief: She uses competitive elections and advocates referendums, opposing attempts to exclude her party.
axes.counterEvidence: Defence of extremist colleagues and praise for Hungary qualify liberal pluralism; democratic procedures are assessed independently of policy content.

axes.brief: Civil-liberty opposition to pandemic restrictions coexists with strong policing and selective restrictions on Islamic dress.
axes.counterEvidence: Defamation litigation and security priorities qualify unconditional speech freedom; earlier March 2020 demands for stronger pandemic measures changed.

axes.brief: She favours German cultural integration and bans on burqas and headscarves, resisting publicly funded parallel communities.
axes.counterEvidence: Her multilingual international life and family do not establish a pluralist public policy; individual lawful assimilation remains possible.

axes.brief: She supports selective skilled migration, tighter asylum and deportation, restricting welfare eligibility for foreign residents.
axes.counterEvidence: Skilled lawful entrants distinguish this from a total ban; refugees’ safety and family reunification are qualified estimates rather than universal rejection.

axes.brief: Interest-driven diplomacy, objections to Ukraine assistance and national defence capacity favour restraint with deterrence.
axes.counterEvidence: Her support for Israeli self-defence and criticism of Russian NATO-airspace violations qualify alignment with every Russian claim.

axes.brief: She wants reduced EU competences and national policy control, allowing exit referendums if reform fails.
axes.counterEvidence: She also advocates reform from inside the EU and qualified her earlier demand for euro exit in 2025; cooperation is not wholly rejected.

qualifications.11: Monetary sovereignty remains an aim even though immediate euro departure was called too late.

axes.brief: Her declared economic liberalism favours privatisation and private enterprise.
axes.counterEvidence: National strategic security and public infrastructure give exceptions; state protection of markets is separate from ownership.

axes.brief: Market competition and international business coexist with strategic national self-interest.
axes.counterEvidence: Opposition to sanctions on Russia is trade openness toward a selected partner, not proof of universal barrier removal.

qualifications.1: Market liberalism and national industry protection compete.

axes.brief: Deregulation, tax cuts and opposition to the minimum wage indicate market coordination.
axes.counterEvidence: Energy and national-security intervention remain exceptions rather than nationwide compulsory production planning.

axes.brief: She opposes inheritance taxation and favours an activating, tightly conditional safety net over expanded transfers.
axes.counterEvidence: Her pensioner and contributory solidarity arguments retain adequate security for eligible citizens; this does not amount to abolishing social insurance.

axes.brief: Civil constitutional authority coexists with invoking a Christian national tradition against established churches’ political positions.
axes.counterEvidence: Agnostic personal identity does not prove secular state preference; Christian cultural recognition does not establish clerical veto.

qualifications.10: Cultural church support and criticism of organised churches’ politics compete.

axes.brief: She opposes same-sex marriage and early sexualisation curricula while accepting civil partnerships and a broader notion of family.
axes.counterEvidence: Her stated family-is-where-children-are position and own adopted children qualify copying the party’s most restrictive household model.

axes.brief: Nuclear energy, industrial production and infrastructure are favoured while selected green technologies and medical mandates are opposed.
axes.counterEvidence: Climate scepticism and dislike of wind turbines are not blanket opposition to technology; enhancement lacks direct evidence.

qualifications.7: Market innovation and distrust of unfamiliar food policy compete.
qualifications.11: Personal choice and medical-risk caution compete.

axes.brief: German federal institutions and national sovereignty suggest protected regional functions with strong national border and security policy.
axes.counterEvidence: Regional election success does not by itself establish secession rights or rejection of all national standards.

qualifications.12: Regional autonomy and common healthcare obligations compete.

axes.brief: Cultural integration and economic incentives explain much of her rhetoric, alongside traditional sex-role assumptions.
axes.counterEvidence: Claims about migrant crime and replacement do not establish a documented genetic explanation; individual biology and social conditions remain competing considerations.

qualifications.2: Inherited national IQ differences are not explicitly established.
qualifications.8: Empathy can be regarded as learned and individually predisposed.
qualifications.14: Cultural and policy explanations qualify assigning a biological racial-violence theory.

religion.reason: She describes herself as agnostic; her partner’s Christianity does not establish her own faith.
